detail: Field-verified 2026-08-04 on plugin 1.24.0: `claude mcp list` printed the command Claude Code actually built from plugin/.mcp.json — in ONE string, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} substituted to the full cache path while ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-} became "". The 1acb0d4 guard therefore evaluated [ -z "" ] → exit 78 every session, for every user of the published plugin; the guard that exists to report an unset root is what unset it. Consequence for all future edits: NEVER use shell parameter-expansion forms other than bare ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in plugin/.mcp.json (or any plugin JSON Claude Code interpolates: hooks.json commands too). Inside launch-server.sh (executed by sh, never interpolated) ${VAR:-} is fine. A regression test in test/hooks/launch-server.test.ts now bans non-bare ${...} forms in plugin/.mcp.json and replays the interpolation. Note the 1acb0d4 verification gap: it tested the string through sh directly, which handles :- correctly — the interpolation layer between the JSON and sh is what any future .mcp.json verification must include.
summary: Claude Code's plugin-config interpolator only understands bare ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} — any other ${...} form (e.g. shell default ${VAR:-}) is replaced with the EMPTY string, not left for sh
